why: The Batch content hash — the first half of a committed Unit's key (ADR 0023 §17), and the thing a retry replays against. Both SDKs must derive it identically from [method, units, params]: canonical JSON, sorted keys, no whitespace, RAW UTF-8 WITH NO HTML ESCAPING, sha256, first 16 hex characters.
measured: 2026-08-27: Go's encoding/json escaped < > & and Python's json.dumps escaped non-ASCII, so the two hashed the same Batch to different keys for every Unit carrying a query string or an accent. The golden that guarded this was pinned on {"url":"a"} and {"depth":2} — plain ASCII with no symbols, the one input class where the two encoders CANNOT differ.

cases.why: a query string — the canonical Unit, and where Go's HTML escaping used to diverge
an ampersand alone, the character Go escaped and Python did not
angle brackets, Go's other two escapes
non-ASCII — the mirror-image bug, escaped by Python and not by Go
an emoji, which is non-ASCII outside the BMP and takes a surrogate pair when escaped
plain ASCII, which NEITHER encoder ever escaped — this row must never change
the Method's name is part of the content: same Units, different Method, different Batch
params are content too: same Units and Method, different params
params key ORDER must not matter — both sides sort
an empty unit list is a Batch, not an error
objects as Units, the shape a real dispatch carries
a Unit object whose VALUE needs escaping, so the escape rule reaches nested strings
nested params, so sorting is recursive rather than top-level only
